## Where I am

- I have not written up the existing results well yet because I pursued better ones.
- I iterated on the probabilistic noise model fit.
- As a result, transfer from synthetic-only data to real data is almost achieved.
- Curriculum training and mixed training results are pending.

## What the noise is

![](assets/real_noise.png){width="94%"}

::: {.notes}
Two real drones, microphone 0, cruise. Both pictures show the same two things: a comb of
horizontal lines over a broadband floor. The lines move when the rotors change speed.
:::

## The model: definition

One rotor $r$ makes lines at multiples of its shaft rate $n_r(t)$. Order $k$ sits at $k\,n_r(t)$.

$$x(t) \;=\; \sum_{r,k} a_{rk}(t)\, s_{rk}(t) \;+\; f(t)$$

$$s_{rk}(t) \;=\; \sqrt{w_k}\,\cos\phi_{rk}(t) \;+\; \sqrt{1-w_k}\,\eta_{rk}(t)$$

$$\phi_{rk}(t) = 2\pi k \!\int_0^{t}\! n_r(\tau)\,d\tau$$

$$w_k = \exp\!\big[-(k/k_{1/2})^2\big], \qquad \gamma_k = \gamma_0 + \gamma_1 k$$

::: {.small}
$a_{rk}$ is line amplitude. It follows a power law in speed: $a \propto (n/n_0)^{p}$, $n_0 = 80$ rev/s.
$w_k$ is the coherent share. $\eta_{rk}$ is narrowband noise of width $\gamma_k$. $f$ is the floor.
:::

::: {.notes}
Fitted per rig: the line powers per (rotor, order), the width law gamma_0 and gamma_1, the
coherence half-order, the floor shape and tilt, the two speed exponents, the per-microphone gains.
:::

## The model: what is optimized

Per clip, on the periodogram $I(f_j)$ of every frame, against the model spectrum $S_\theta(f_j)$:

$$\hat\theta \;=\; \arg\min_{\theta}\; \mathcal{W}(\theta) \;-\; \log p(\theta)$$

$$\mathcal{W}(\theta) \;=\; \sum_{j}\left[\frac{I(f_j)}{S_\theta(f_j)} + \log S_\theta(f_j)\right] \quad \text{(Whittle)}$$

::: {.small}
The Whittle term is exact for a Gaussian process observed on a fine frequency grid. Its expected
value is minimal only at $S_\theta = S^{*}$, the true spectrum.

$p(\theta)$ holds the priors: smooth floor shape, bounded widths, bounded speed exponents.
:::

::: {.notes}
This is a MAP estimate, not a full posterior. The rotor speeds are taken from telemetry and are
not fitted.
:::

## The model, in one figure

![](assets/model_anatomy.png){width="84%"}

::: {.small}
Each rotor makes a comb of lines at multiples of its shaft rate. A broadband floor sits under the comb.
The lines follow the telemetry, so the comb moves with the flight.
:::

::: {.notes}
The fitted quantities, in the order they act: line power per rotor and order, the line width law,
the coherent share per order, the floor shape on control frequencies, the floor tilt.
:::

## How the fit works

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="32%"}
**1. Bench**

One motor. Constant speed. Six setpoints from 50 to 90 rev/s. This fixes the line shape and the width law.
:::
::: {.column width="32%"}
**2. Michael's rig**

Four rotors. Cruise clips and a standby clip. Rotor speeds come from the telemetry, so the comb is driven, not assumed.
:::
::: {.column width="32%"}
**3. DREGON**

The same model family, refitted on flight audio. The bench fit is carried over as the starting point.
:::
::::

::: {.small}
Each clip is fitted on its own by MAP with a Whittle likelihood. Within one rig the fits are then
tied. Every clip of that rig shares the line power per order, the width law, the coherent share,
the floor shape, the floor tilt, both speed exponents. Only three things move per clip: the
per-rotor gain, the floor level, the coherence half-order.
::::

![](../../../docs/explainers/flight-startup/blend_weights.png){width="56%"}

::: {.small}
A rig with several clips keeps one fit per operating point. At playback the fits are blended by
mean rotor speed. The blend is exactly silent at zero speed.
:::

::: {.small}
Twelve draws: eight at the measured width, four at twice that width. The widths come from the

further than twice the real drone-to-drone difference. None of the eight was rejected.
:::

## Transfer result: both clouds

| Training noise | best round | saved checkpoint |
|:--|--:|--:|
| Real flights (`real_r4_scv2_unified`) | **2.99** (r48) | **3.11** (r24) |
| Hard cloud (`rig_hard_scv2_unified`) | **5.37** (r102) | **5.41** (r124) |
| Easy cloud (`rig_easy_scv2_unified`) | **5.72** (r29) | **6.09** (r57) |
| Previous fitted presets (`rig_fitted_scv2_unified`) | 9.97 (r23) | — |
| Wide hand-set ranges (`ctrl_diverse_scv2_unified`) | 14.27 (r4) | — |

::: {.small}
Real-split PIT MAE in rev/s. The left column is the best validation round. The right column is the
file the selection rule saved, which uses a median-smoothed score.

Synthetic-only training reaches 5.4 rev/s on real drones. The previous fitted presets reached 10.0.
The hard cloud matches the easy cloud. Neither real rig is likely in the hard cloud.
:::

::: {.notes}
Both arms degrade after their best round: easy 5.72 to 7.91, hard 5.37 to 6.23. Checkpoint
selection matters.
:::
